definitions.explanation: An object kept as a reminder of a deceased person or someone who has departed. Carries a strong emotional connotation of loss and remembrance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{形見|かたみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{指輪|ゆびわ}→指輪：01744_yubiwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧にして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I treasure the ring my grandmother left me as a keepsake.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{時計|とけい}→時計：00677_tokei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{亡|な}き⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{形見|かたみ}だ。
examples.english: This watch is a memento of my late father.

examples.japanese: {形見|かたみ}{分|わ}けで、⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{姉妹|しまい}→姉妹：03201_shimai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{分|わ}けた→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧。
examples.english: In dividing up the keepsakes, my sisters and I shared our mother's kimonos.

notes:
USAGE:
Unlike the English "memento" or "souvenir," {形見|かたみ} specifically refers to an object left behind by someone who has died or permanently departed. It is not used for souvenirs from trips or gifts between living people. The compound {形見|かたみ}{分|わ}け refers to the custom of distributing a deceased person's belongings among family and close friends as keepsakes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {形見|かたみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{品|しな}→品：03192_shina⟧: keepsake item
- {形見|かたみ}{分|わ}け: distributing keepsakes of the deceased
- 〜⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{形見|かたみ}: memento of (someone deceased)
